rule_text: Every workflow and required workflow step has exactly one accountable owner.
A creator cannot be the sole final independent reviewer of the same consequential output.
No AI role may approve or alter a founder-reserved decision.

rule_name: Canonical identity only for new work
rule_text: All new workflow ownership and state writes use canonical active identities; aliases are input/history compatibility only.
Inactive, merged-away or unknown identities cannot own or execute current work.
Business objects and workflow runs may move only through declared state transitions.
A step cannot start or complete before all required predecessor outputs and gates pass.
A receiving owner may reject an incomplete handoff; incomplete handoffs cannot be treated as accepted.
No workflow may close while a mandatory step, blocker, obligation or handoff remains unresolved.
Completed decisions, reviews, acceptances, revisions and attempts are never overwritten; changes create new versions/records.
Supplier-facing payloads, files, portal views and notifications may not contain customer identity before the approved reveal state.
No supplier assignment or notification may be created without an approved immutable supplier-safe package.
No inquiry may be dispatched while mandatory qualification, route, document or readiness blockers remain.
Proposed, ambiguous, rejected or excluded routes cannot independently authorize supplier dispatch.
Only currently approved, eligible suppliers may receive a dispatch assignment.
One supplier may receive at most one assignment for the same inquiry version and dispatch scope.
Refused or failed assignments are not counted as contacted and do not create success notifications.
The platform may normalize for comparison but cannot alter the supplier's original quotation revision.
Customers may see only their own approved/published quotation comparison versions.
Supplier contact identity is revealed only after the founder-approved payment state is confirmed and reconciled.
The reveal charge uses the current founder-approved reveal-fee policy; changing the percentage is founder-reserved.
QuotesDone does not charge suppliers a job-success commission unless the founder changes the commercial model.
The founder-approved founding-supplier exemption is permanent for eligible suppliers and cannot be recalculated by mutable counts.
Supplier subscription amount, start date and exemption policy are founder-reserved.
Terms acceptance must reference the exact displayed version and hash and remain append-only.
No legal acceptance certificate may be generated before a valid acceptance record exists.
Every extracted document fact, normalization, score and review finding must retain source/version provenance.
Missing technical, quantity, regulatory or document facts remain unknown and trigger clarification/escalation.
Conflicting evidence is preserved and cannot be silently overwritten by lower-authority evidence.
Supplier onboarding cannot approve its own supplier; verification is an independent review.
The effective identity executing a monetary action cannot independently reconcile/approve that same action.
External payment/refund events are unique, authenticated and safe under duplicate or out-of-order delivery.
Unknown, conflicting or unreconciled monetary states are blocked/quarantined and cannot be treated as success.
Notifications must respect consent, opt-out, suppression, frequency and sender-policy rules.
Marketing or operational content may publish only the exact independently approved revision.
Visual/video/file review must inspect the actual final artifact, not only the prompt or brief.
An agent, department or builder cannot independently certify its own consequential behavior or change.
Product/engineering/AI implementers cannot issue the final release go/no-go.
No consequential production release is approved without a defined and executable rollback/recovery path.
Reports and forecasts use canonical metric definitions and source lineage.
Managers may not declare success solely from activity or vanity metrics when a business outcome is defined.
Analysis and decisions must distinguish fact, assumption, inference, confidence and unresolved uncertainty.
Policy exceptions require an explicit authorized decision and cannot bypass privacy, safety or founder boundaries.
Every externally waiting or time-bound step has a deadline, reminder/escalation owner and terminal state.
Retries preserve the failed first attempt and use a new attempt record linked to the original.
Cancellation preserves the business record, reason, authority and prior evidence.
Role, department, reporting or reviewer changes require a formal Phase A change request and founder approval.
Category overlays provide qualification and comparison expertise but cannot approve suppliers, dispatch, reveal identity or change policy.
Specialist and document handoffs do not transfer overall inquiry accountability away from RFQ Qualification Manager unless an explicit approved workflow says so.
Customer comparison uses the canonical normalized quote records and published version, not multiple conflicting comparison implementations.
All supplier assignments and notifications originate from the canonical W12 dispatch batch.
Reveal payment, billing and reconciliation use the canonical transaction lifecycle and not parallel monetary states.

rule_name: No workflow activation in Phase B
rule_text: Phase B may define and reconcile workflows but cannot activate new automation, provider calls or autonomous execution.

rule_name: Zero paid inference in Phase B
rule_text: Phase B uses no OpenRouter or paid model calls.
